neighbours.label: Subject-start word (determiner/demonstrative/noun like 'these', 'each', 'today', 'the trend') right after a causal connective 'so' / 'therefore,' where a main verb is expected next
fire: The trail was muddy after the storm, so each hiker carried an extra pair of socks.
Prices for lumber doubled over the summer; therefore, these new houses cost far more than planned.
She had already seen the film twice, so tonight she chose a documentary instead.
The old recipe used too much salt, so the updated version cuts it by half.
Interest rates rose sharply in the spring; therefore, many buyers postponed their mortgage applications.
The printer jammed again, so that report is still sitting unfinished on my desk.
Snow blocked the mountain pass for a week, and so the village relied on its stored grain.
The data were collected from only one hospital; therefore, our findings may not generalize to other settings.
quiet: The trail was so muddy after the storm that half the group turned back early.
Prices for lumber doubled over the summer, according to a report from the builders' association.
She had already seen the film twice and still laughed at every single joke.
The old recipe used too much salt, and nobody in the family seemed to mind.
Interest rates rose sharply in the spring, catching many first-time buyers completely off guard.
The printer jammed again, so badly that the technician had to open the whole case.
Snow blocked the mountain pass for a week during the coldest January anyone could remember.
The data were collected from only one hospital, so far as the authors were able to tell.
